title: Irreducible components become geometrically irreducible after a finite separable extension of the base field
author: The Stacks Project Authors
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: For X locally of finite type over k with finitely many irreducible components, the lemma produces a finite separable extension k'/k such that every irreducible component of X_{k'} is geometrically irreducible over k' (statement lines 1847-1855). The proof descends the finiteness of the set of components to the separable closure using the Galois orbit statement for components, so that the components over the closure form a finite list, and then applies the definability statement for components of the base change to descend each of them to a common finite extension (proof lines 1858-1867). The claim is H2: two parts of a single cited lemma combined with the finiteness hypothesis, with the common finite extension for all components as the point of the argument.
